extracted.intended_audience: DOE communications staff, press officers, public affairs offices, and contractors who draft DOE press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and formatting press releases for the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), following DOE-specific style priorities, federal plain-language requirements, accessibility standards, and content requirements for funding, research, and policy announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style Hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: Order of authority for stylistic questions: 1. EERE Style Guide / CMEI Style Guide (DOE-specific) 2. Associated Press Stylebook 3. Merriam-Webster's Dictionary 4. Chicago Manual of Style
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When conflicts arise, follow the top-most applicable source; DOE/EERE/CMEI exceptions to AP are permitted where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain Language Requirements (Plain Language Act of 2010)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear language federal agencies must use; active voice; avoid acronyms where possible; define necessary acronyms on first use; reading level: Grade 8 or below; short sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write for an eighth-grade reading level, minimize jargon, define any acronym at first use, and prefer short, direct sentences to improve comprehension for broad public audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Use active voice: e.g., 'DOE awarded $X to...' (not 'X was awarded by DOE'). Ensure a clear subject in every sentence and direct attribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer constructions where DOE (or named actor) is the grammatical subject performing the action; avoid passive constructions that obscure responsibility or delay clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE-Specific Style (names and acronyms)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Department of Energy" first reference; "DOE" or "the department" subsequent; full names of programs first reference; use standard acronyms (EIA, NREL, NETL, etc.); national laboratory names: full name first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On first mention, spell out formal program and organization names; after first use, the standard acronym may be used. Follow DOE-preferred forms for lab and program names rather than AP defaults when DOE guidance differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press Release Required Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Required elements for press releases: plain language summary (lead); specific funding amounts; cited research papers (if applicable); lab/researcher attribution; public benefit articulated; Section 508 accessibility; ADA-compliant (alt text, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every release should include a clear lead summarizing the news in plain language, precise dollar figures when funding is involved, proper attribution to labs/researchers, explicit statement of public benefit, and meet accessibility standards (alt text for images, readable structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required for Funding Announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding announcement requirements: specific dollar amount; funding source (program, grant); recipient (named); project description; expected outcomes; performance period; total project value (incl. cost share); impact metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide fully transparent financial and project details: name the recipient(s), identify the funding program or grant, include exact amounts, list project timeframe and expected measurable impacts, and disclose total project value including any leveraging or cost share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required for Research Releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Research release requirements: lab affiliation; funding source; cite peer-reviewed paper (if published); plain language explanation; energy/economic implications; photographs of researchers/equipment; researcher availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When releasing research news, always connect the work to the lab and funder, cite publications, explain significance in plain language and potential energy/economic impacts, include visuals with captions and alt text, and make researchers available for media inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required for Policy/Program Releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Policy/program release requirements: specific policy details; effective dates; affected populations; stakeholder benefits; implementation plan; comment periods (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly describe what the policy does, when it takes effect, who it affects, how stakeholders will benefit or be affected, how implementation will occur, and provide details on any public comment opportunities and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language (Grade 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write content at a Grade 8 reading level to ensure broad public comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short sentences, common words, and straightforward explanations; avoid technical jargon or explain it in plain terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor active constructions where the actor (DOE, a named person, or organization) is the subject performing the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example guidance: 'DOE awarded $X to...' instead of passive equivalents; this supports clarity and direct attribution throughout the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific amounts/dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Include precise dollar amounts and specific dates where relevant in announcements and timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague terms like 'millions' or 'soon'—provide exact figures and calendar dates (or clearly defined performance periods) to ensure transparency and journalistic utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP style (with DOE exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow Associated Press (AP) style as the general standard, except where DOE/EERE/CMEI guidance provides specific exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AP capitalization, number, and attribution conventions unless DOE-specific guidance requires a deviation; consult the style hierarchy when uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: National lab/program names correct
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure national laboratory and program names are correct and use full names on first reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm official lab and program names (use DOE-preferred spellings) and include the full name on first mention, followed by the accepted short form or acronym.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment language present
rubrics_metrics.description: Include required acknowledgment language (e.g., identifying funding sources or program acknowledgments) where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use any prescribed boilerplate or acknowledgment phrases required by the funding program or DOE guidance to ensure contractual and publicity obligations are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases must comply with Section 508 accessibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure content for screen readers, provide alt text for images, use accessible fonts and color contrast, and ensure documents and attachments (PDFs, etc.) are accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disclaimers
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any required disclaimers or legal notices applicable to the release content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add standard legal or funding disclaimers per DOE policy or grant terms; consult communications policy to determine necessary boilerplate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cited peer-reviewed source (research)
rubrics_metrics.description: For research releases, cite peer-reviewed publications when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full citations or links to published articles so reporters and the public can verify and read the underlying research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public benefit clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate the public benefit of the action, funding, research, or policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state how the work benefits taxpayers, improves energy outcomes, advances technology, or otherwise serves public interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized spokespersons quoted
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotes from authorized DOE spokespersons or relevant officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prepared quotations that provide perspective, context, or reaction from named officials; ensure quoted persons are cleared to speak on the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinated with affected stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate messaging with affected stakeholders prior to release when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage internal and external stakeholders (e.g., labs, program offices, partner organizations) to ensure accuracy, permissions for use of names/quotes, and timing alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing aligns with policy/program launch
rubrics_metrics.description: Schedule release timing to align with policy or program launches and related events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate release dates to ensure announcements do not pre-empt or conflict with implementation timelines or partner communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia (photos of facilities, researchers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include multimedia such as photos of facilities or researchers where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality images with captions and alt text; secure photo release permissions and ensure images comply with accessibility and branding guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal communications policy compliant
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure releases comply with applicable federal communications policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm compliance with federal rules on publicity, information dissemination, and any program-specific communication restrictions; consult legal or policy leads when necessary.
